prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t a single universally “best” roofing company for Dallas — the right contractor depends on your needs (residential vs. commercial, budget, insurance work, warranty preferences). Instead of one name, I can help you find the best option for your situation. Below are practical steps and a quick checklist to identify a top roofer in Dallas.

How to find the best Dallas roofer for your replacement
- Look for credentials: licensed in Texas, insured (liability + workers’ comp), and bonded if required.  
- Manufacturer certifications: GAF Master Elite, Owens Corning Preferred, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, etc. These mean they meet quality and training standards and can give enhanced warranties.  
- Local reputation: check Google Reviews, Yelp, BBB (A+ rating), and recent references. Look for consistent recent reviews, not just old ones.  
- Experience with your roof type and with insurance claims if you’re filing one.  
- Written estimate: detailed scope, materials (brand/line), tear-off vs. overlays, ventilation, underlayment, drip edge, flashing, cleanup, timeline, total cost, and payment schedule.  
- Warranties: both manufacturer and workmanship. Get them in writing and know who services the warranty (contractor vs. manufacturer).  
- Permits and inspections: contractor should pull permits and arrange inspections when required.  
- Payment terms: avoid large upfront cash-only demands. Typical is a modest deposit, progress payments, final payment after completion and satisfied inspection.

Questions to ask each contractor
- Are you licensed and insured in Texas? Can you provide proof?  
- Are you a certified installer for any shingle/roof manufacturer? Which ones?  
- Do you have local references I can contact?  
- Will you pull permits and handle inspections?  
- What is included in the written warranty? Is it transferable?  
- Who will supervise the job and who is my point of contact?  
- What’s your cleanup plan and timeline?  

Red flags
- High-pressure sales tactics or “storm-chaser” claims (contractors who follow storms offering quick deals).  
- No physical local address or no verifiable references.  
- Requests for large full payment up front or cash-only deals.  
- Vague written estimates or no contract.

If you want, I can:
- Provide a short vetted list of reputable Dallas roofers (I’ll need your ZIP code and whether it’s residential/commercial).  
- Draft an email or phone script with the questions above to send to contractors.  
- Help compare 3 estimates side-by-side if you get quotes.

Which would you prefer?
